skipSemantics: May-skip, not must-skip: a listed test that runs and passes on a machine where its precondition holds is green. Matching is exact on the pre-'(' portion of the TRX result testName (xunit theory rows serialize with arguments, e.g. Class.Method(x: 1)); a name with no parens matches whole. Anchor is the TRX result list, never Counters arithmetic.
admissionRule: allowedSkips is not a quarantine list. A test may be listed only when its precondition is a property of the machine or OS that cannot be satisfied by configuration during a contract run, and its change names the machine class where it executes. Two named PERMANENT BANS apply: (1) CcpClient.Tests.DataRootOverrideTests.DefaultSettingsPath_EnvUnset_IsThePlatformDefault must never be allowed to skip because a process-wide CCP_DATA_ROOT override makes the floor vacuous; (2) CcpClient.Tests.ChaosTunnelLoopbackTests.Logging_RouteClassesOnly_NeverFilenameOrQuery must be fixed at the source, never quarantined.
bumpRule: Bump total only in the same commit as the test change that moves the count, with the reason recorded here. Never widen, disable, or special-case a check to make a step pass. Adding a name to allowedSkips requires the admission rule above and the machine class where it executes.
lastMovedBy: Merged lane/haptic-provider-set-v2: BOTH provider routes admitted together, over a CompositeHapticSink, with the three owner decisions the first audit's STOP was raised for. +21 unit, +1 headless. THE PROBE IS GATED: CapabilityRegistry.RunAllAsync probes every registered capability at launch, so registering the sink ungated meant a default install fired an HTTP GET at 127.0.0.1:20010 on EVERY launch for a feature whose master toggle was off. The gate is upstream's own auto-connect conjunction field for field (App.xaml.cs:2176, predicate :3580-3589) and lives in one expression a fact can call; when it refuses it answers the EXISTING not-probed arm, never a server-unreachable answer, which would be a claim about a socket it deliberately did not open. BOTH ROUTE FLAGS DEFAULT FALSE, which is upstream's stored default (HapticSettings.cs:769 has no initializer), and the two provider checkboxes ship with them so the refusal is actionable instead of naming a control that does not exist. THE CROSS-ROUTE DEDUPE IS DELETED: it keyed on the RAW device id across routes, and since Buttplug ids are bare indices and Lovense ids are JSON property names, a collision silently dropped a real device from the list a user reads to find their toy - upstream dedupes on NAME precisely because Buttplug ids are session-scoped. TWO BUGS FOUND WHILE PROVING IT, neither in the brief: Confirmed and Available had silently diverged, so an observation carrying both a refusal and a device list reported Confirmed while classifying Unavailable - two answers about one observation, in the type whose whole purpose is that there is one; and UnadmittedHapticSink had no disposed guard on ObserveAsync at all. Every new fact is mutation-checked: re-inserting the dedupe reds exactly the colliding-ids fact, and awaiting the routes' stops sequentially reds exactly the parallel-dispatch fact - which is proved by a SIGNAL, not a clock, so there is no sleep, no delay and no clock read anywhere in it. No test opens a socket to a real haptic server and the haptic suite still runs in about three seconds. CcpClient.Tests 2673 to 2694, CcpClient.HeadlessTests 154 to 155.
